heading: Laravel is more than CRUD, routes, and Blade
intro: Once you stay with Laravel long enough, it starts to feel more like a city than a single framework. There is a runtime core, a feature-building layer, a package ecosystem, debugging tools, deployment concerns, and long-term maintenance work. This overview exists so you can see that whole shape before diving into the topic sites one by one.

items.title: Foundation layer: how Laravel handles a request
items.body: This is where you learn routes, controllers, middleware, Blade, validation, migrations, models, and the baseline rhythm of a Laravel application.

items.title: Application layer: how code stays readable as the project grows
items.body: As the app becomes less trivial, you start needing service classes, policies, form requests, actions, queues, cache, and better boundaries for business logic.

items.title: Ecosystem layer: packages, tools, and real runtime environments
items.body: Composer, vendor, npm, Vite, Sail, Redis, Horizon, testing, logging, and deployment all live here. This is the layer that moves Laravel beyond tutorial mode and closer to real application work.

items.title: Expansion layer: what real products eventually run into
items.body: APIs, uploads, search, realtime behavior, team workflows, roles or permissions, third-party integrations, and performance pressure usually arrive once the product starts meeting real users.

items.title: A short practical starting point if you are returning to Laravel
items.body: Instead of reading randomly, run one small command flow and map each step to the relevant topic pages in this portal.
items.code:
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate
npm install
npm run dev
php artisan route:list
bullets: If you get stuck at `composer install`, jump to `Composer & vendor`.
If `key:generate`, `migrate`, or `route:list` still feel fuzzy, jump to `PHP Commands & Artisan`.
If you get blocked at `npm install` or `npm run dev`, jump to `Node, npm, and the frontend layer around Laravel`.
Once the app is running, continue with `App structure`, `Request flow`, and `Blade & UI` to reconnect the full picture.
items.note: A good overview page should not only say how broad Laravel is. It should also give you a concrete enough entry path so you can restart without feeling lost.
